headline: 204 g/t GOLD AT FRUTA DEL NORTE — Lundin's Quebrada Dorada Epithermal Vein Extends to 8 km; Biggest FDN Exploration Program Ever Underway
snippet: Lundin Gold (TSX: LUG) released drilling results from the Fruta del Norte mine in Ecuador on September 24, with drill hole BLP-2026-553 returning 204.26 g/t gold over 3.05 metres from 140.25 metres — the highest-grade interval ever recorded at the deposit. The new Quebrada Dorada epithermal vein discovery extends the known gold-mineralised trend at FDN to more than eight kilometres; the largest exploration program in the mine's history is now underway, with the Bonza Sur corridor and adjacent Quebrada Dorada system together pointing to a multi-system, multi-million-ounce district that management says is not yet fully understood.

headline: 176 g/t GOLD IN RED LAKE — West Red Lake Drills Previously Unmined 200x200m Zone; 925 g/t Over 1m Inside Austin 955 Complex
snippet: West Red Lake Gold Mines (TSXV: WRLG) reported drill results from the Madsen Mine in Ontario's Red Lake District on September 24, with the Austin 955 Complex returning 176.04 g/t Au over 5.3 metres (including 1m at 925.52 g/t Au), and the Austin 904 Complex — a rare intact, previously unmined 200-by-200-metre panel at approximately 600 metres depth — cutting 35.72 g/t Au over 13.35 metres. Management says full access to the 904 panel is expected to enable larger stopes and improved extraction efficiency as the results are integrated into the 2027 mine plan.

headline: CENTINELA STRIKE VOTE OPENS SEPTEMBER 26 — 730 Antofagasta Workers Ballot Alongside Escondida Suspension; Copper Has Two Open Fronts
snippet: Two unions representing approximately 730 workers at Antofagasta Minerals' Centinela copper mine in Chile announced a strike authorisation ballot running September 26-28 after wage negotiations reached a "dead end" — with core grievances centring on structural pay discrimination across equivalent roles, making a one-time bonus unlikely to resolve the impasse. Under Chilean law, if workers vote yes, mandatory five-day government mediation follows before any legal walkout; the unions stated they are "financially prepared" for a prolonged action, opening the earliest possible walkout window in early October. Combined with BHP's operational suspension at Escondida following a fatality, two of Chile's largest copper operations are now simultaneously under labour and safety risk.

headline: BONANZA GRADE IN GOLDEN TRIANGLE: 166 g/t AU + 3,383 g/t AG OVER 3.1m — Cambria Expands Premier Infill Program to 42,000m
snippet: Cambria Gold Mines (TSXV: CAMB) reported drill results from the Premier Gold Project near Stewart in northwestern British Columbia on September 22, highlighted by hole P26U-0095 cutting 166.22 g/t Au and 3,383 g/t Ag over 3.1 metres — including a 1.1-metre sub-interval grading 467 g/t Au and 9,510 g/t Ag — within a 6,923-metre, 70-hole batch. Coverage published today by North of 60 Mining News notes that Cambria simultaneously expanded the Premier Mine Complex infill program to 42,000 planned metres, scaling up after consistently strong early results in the high-grade vein system at this historic BC gold-silver mine.

headline: DENISON JOINT VENTURE WRAPS HOOK-CARTER SUMMER PROGRAM — Derkson Corridor Prioritised for 2027 Drilling in Athabasca Basin
snippet: Greenridge Exploration (TSXV) completed its summer 2026 exploration program at the Hook-Carter Uranium Project in Saskatchewan's southwestern Athabasca Basin on September 24, executed in partnership with Denison Mines. The work will provide tighter drill-hole targeting along the Derkson Corridor — identified as the project's primary uranium-bearing structural trend — ahead of a planned 2027 drill campaign, positioning the joint venture at a time when Athabasca Basin uranium exploration is accelerating alongside uranium term prices at all-time highs above $96/lb.

headline: AUSTRALIA BREAKS GROUND ON FIRST DOMESTIC NdPr OXIDE PLANT — Arafura Nolans Project In Construction; 2029 First Production Target
snippet: Arafura Rare Earths (ASX: ARU) commenced construction at the Nolans Rare Earths Project in Australia's Northern Territory in September 2026, making it the first fully integrated mine-to-NdPr-oxide project to reach construction in Australia. The company confirmed the 37-month build timeline is on schedule, with site reinstatement complete and project financing contractual close expected in October 2026; Arafura has also locked in 1,000 tonnes of NdPr offtake, positioning Nolans as a critical non-Chinese source of the neodymium-praseodymium oxide used in permanent magnets for EVs, wind turbines and defence hardware.

headline: 8,760 COUNTS PER SECOND — Purepoint Uranium's Q24 Hits Basement Uranium Over 7.4m at Dorado JV; New Athabasca Vector Confirmed
snippet: Purepoint Uranium Group reported encouraging results from the first hole into the new Q24 target at the Dorado joint venture in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin on September 22, cutting a 7.4-metre radioactive interval averaging 8,760 counts per second directly at the unconformity — the geologic horizon where unconformity-style uranium ore, including Cigar Lake and McArthur River, is concentrated. The Q24 intercept opens a new discovery vector on the Dorado property at a time when the structural uranium supply deficit and record term prices are driving intense exploration activity across the Athabasca Basin.

headline: LITHIUM FALLS TO $19.83/kg — Why September's Price Correction Is Less Bearish Than Headlines Suggest
snippet: Analysis published in late September 2026 argues that lithium's retreat to approximately $19.83/kg is less structurally bearish than current price action implies: CATL's Jianxiawo mine — China's largest by capacity — has had its environmental impact approval revoked and is back on care and maintenance, quietly removing an estimated 30,500 tonnes of LCE from the 2026 supply forecast. Global battery demand surpassed 1.5 TWh for the first time in 2025 and continues to grow, driven by EVs, grid-scale storage and AI-adjacent hardware; the piece frames current price weakness as a temporary inventory correction rather than a structural multi-year bear phase.

headline: SILVER OUTLOOK: THE OCTOBER HIKE IS PRICED IN — THE POSITIONING ISN'T; $63 Floor in Focus Before Structural Deficit Reasserts
snippet: An analysis from GoldSilver.com in late September 2026 argues that while the market has repriced a Federal Reserve October rate hike to 77% probability — weighing on silver near $64 — speculative positioning has not yet reset to reflect the new rate environment, setting up a sharper-than-expected bounce once leveraged long liquidation runs its course. The piece identifies silver's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, record industrial demand from solar and EV manufacturing, and de-dollarisation buying as fundamentals that have not changed; the current pullback is characterised as a positioning flush ahead of the next structural leg higher.

headline: GOLD SELLOFF OR BULL BREAKOUT? — Vermeulen Sees $4,200 as Critical Line; Short-Term Signals Turn Bullish, Long-Term Caution Remains
snippet: Technical analyst Chris Vermeulen, writing for Sprott Money in September 2026, presents a mixed outlook after gold's selloff to $4,268: shorter-duration charts are turning tentatively bullish off the recent low, but longer-term indicators still warrant caution, with $4,200 identified as critical structural support before the next potential rally leg. Vermeulen's analysis contextualises the current move within gold's 2026 arc — from roughly $3,900 at year-start to a January record of $5,589, correcting 23% since — and recommends that investors in junior miners wait for a decisive breakout above $4,400 before adding speculative exposure.
